title: Single-tenant enterprise with regional data and operating requirements

scope.description: Fictional Alder enterprise: 4,800 workforce identities, one Entra tenant, EU and US applications, one hybrid AD source and regionally delegated operations. No actual organization, tenant, user or deployment was inspected.
outOfScope: A legally mandated independent identity authority
Production sign-in, emergency access or recovery execution
assumptions: The fictional legal owner accepts a common corporate identity/control-plane failure domain.
Regional requirements concern specified data/telemetry and delegated operations, not a requirement for separate tenants.
The proposed emergency and recovery paths still need Entra and reachable management APIs.
No real legal, licensing, availability, cost or recovery determination is made.

One synthetic legacy cohort temporarily retains primary federation while its app dependency is reviewed; active PHS is the preferred end state where acceptable. Backup-only hashes require the separate R2 activation/sign-in/return exercise.

sourceFacts.fact: A tenant is an administrative/configuration boundary; additional tenants need a specific unmet requirement. Regional labels alone do not prove one is needed.
sourceFacts.scopeLimit: This fictional enterprise's common-identity acceptance is a scenario assumption, not a legal finding.

requirements.text: Use the existing single tenant if the remaining mandatory requirements can be met; regional teams receive scoped application/data administration, not independent identity authority.
acceptance: Document why each requirement can fit within one tenant.
No additional tenant is justified by region count alone.
unknowns: Actual scoped delegation and service fit are not inspected.

requirements.text: Keep fictional EU customer payloads and raw security telemetry in approved EU storage/processing locations for 365 days; central analysts may receive a redacted incident summary only.
acceptance: Per-service storage, processing, backup and telemetry flows mapped.
Cross-region raw export denied; summary fields approved by the data owner.
unknowns: Service-specific geography, retention and export behavior require legal/product verification.

requirements.text: Regain approved emergency administration within 30 minutes if the normal hybrid path fails while Entra and target management services remain available.
acceptance: Two fresh independently controlled cloud-only emergency sign-ins.
Every use/action observed by monitoring and the allowed operation reversed.
unknowns: No emergency account, independent method or alert has been exercised.

requirements.text: Prefer active PHS where acceptable. For the temporarily federated approved synthetic legacy cohort, activate the prepared PHS cloud authentication path within 60 minutes and keep last synchronized password/state age within 24 hours.
acceptance: Explicit activation/routing and fresh positive/negative sign-ins observed.
Measured propagation, password/state age and rollback meet the fictional objectives.
unknowns: PHS legality, configuration, sync health, activation and rollback are untested.

requirements.text: Restore approved scoped tenant configuration within four hours from a trusted external baseline no older than 24 hours, including dependent relationships and explicit native-restore gaps.
acceptance: Trusted baseline retained outside the exercised tenant's administration.
Object and directed relationship diffs plus fresh allow/deny tests pass.
unknowns: Coverage, retention, actual baseline custody and RTO/RPO not observed.

requirements.text: Determine whether the fictional EU workload needs exclusive local cryptographic authority beyond ordinary service encryption/customer-managed-key options before any sovereignty claim.
acceptance: Legal owner signs a separate key/processing/operator/recovery authority determination.
Selected service coverage and residual vendor/recovery-key access documented.
unknowns: The key authority requirement is intentionally unresolved; residency is not substituted for it.

requirements.text: Privileged humans use phishing-resistant protected administration; CI workload identities cannot grant themselves tenant-wide roles or alter the recovery baseline.
acceptance: Normal, elevated, emergency, workload and baseline-custody paths are distinct.
Directed CI→app permissions stop at the application scope; forbidden escalation tests deny.
unknowns: Credential, permission and revocation enforcement is design-only.

requirements.text: Office services tolerate cloud sign-in unavailability without autonomous local production; local incident contacts and retained evidence remain usable for the declared S1 boundary.
acceptance: Loss of cloud identity stops new affected cloud sessions; no S3 claim.
Offline contact list and independent baseline/evidence retrieval are exercised before reliance.
unknowns: No continuity or retrieval timing observed.

boundaries.crossingRule: No second tenant unless a documented mandatory requirement cannot fit.

contains: Hybrid AD source and cloud workforce identities
boundaries.crossingRule: Sync supplies identity/password state; runtime cloud fallback requires activation and verified freshness.
App/data delegation does not confer tenant/key/baseline administration.
Separate storage, processing, operator, key, telemetry and recovery determinations; no legal inference from geography.
Raw EU records do not cross; approved summaries exclude identifiers and raw payload.
Network location grants no implicit privilege; cloud reachability remains required.
Application authorization is enforced separately from workforce Conditional Access.
No industrial safety or autonomous site requirement is asserted.

edges.permission: Read only approved source identity/password synchronization scope.
edges.credential: Dedicated connector identity with protected locally held connector material.
edges.delegation: Hybrid identity owner grants connector scope, not tenant administration.

revocation.mechanism: Disable connector identity and remove source scope; reconcile already synchronized identities separately.
revocation.residualAccess: Previously synchronized cloud credentials/objects are not removed by stopping sync.

edges.permission: Update only designated synchronized workforce attributes/password state.
edges.credential: Approved synchronization connector credential; no export in this record.
edges.delegation: Tenant owner authorizes exact sync capability.

revocation.mechanism: Disable connector authorization, isolate affected objects and reconcile cloud sign-ins.
revocation.residualAccess: Cloud hashes, sessions and already granted access can persist.

edges.permission: Time-bounded approved identity/policy administration under least-privilege roles.
edges.credential: Cloud admin identity with phishing-resistant method on protected workstation.
edges.delegation: Normal elevated role activation; not the emergency bootstrap.

revocation.mechanism: Remove role, disable affected identity, revoke applicable sessions and verify resource denial.
revocation.latencyLimit: 15-minute proposed incident objective; measured per service before reliance.
revocation.residualAccess: Existing tokens/service state require separate verification.

edges.permission: Permanent-active Global Administrator emergency authority; execute only incident-approved operations, with exceptional use monitored. This is not normal just-in-time elevation.
edges.credential: Two cloud-only .onmicrosoft.com identities with separately controlled supported phishing-resistant emergency methods and reviewed blocking-policy exclusions.
edges.delegation: Tenant owner pre-establishes emergency authority and offline custody.

revocation.mechanism: Contain a compromised emergency identity/method only after verifying another usable emergency path; reconcile sessions.
revocation.latencyLimit: Incident-specific; no blanket instant revocation claim.
revocation.residualAccess: Entra, method support and target control plane remain common dependencies.

edges.permission: Issue application-scoped identity assertions; app still decides permitted operations.
edges.credential: Service-issued audience-bound tokens accepted by the application's configured trust.
edges.delegation: Application owner configures exact issuer/audience and group/app-role mapping.

revocation.mechanism: Remove app assignment/trust and block at app policy; reconcile valid token/session lifetimes.
revocation.residualAccess: Token expiry and app session revocation may differ.

edges.permission: Manage regional application role assignments and data handling only.
edges.credential: Phishing-resistant delegated human identity, app-scoped role.
edges.delegation: App owner approves regional scope; no tenant role grant.

revocation.mechanism: Remove app role, invalidate app session and test region-scoped denial.
revocation.residualAccess: No effect on previously exported data; export controls separate.

edges.permission: Deploy reviewed application package to one regional environment; no tenant role or data-reader grant.
edges.credential: Environment-bound managed identity or narrow issuer/subject/audience workload federation.
edges.delegation: Application owner approves deployment subject and environment.

revocation.mechanism: Disable deployment binding, remove resource permission and block pending deployment.
revocation.residualAccess: Previously deployed code must also be assessed/rolled back.

edges.permission: Read/write only purpose-bound EU payload and append regional logs under data policy.
edges.credential: Application-managed identity scoped to EU stores.
edges.delegation: EU data owner grants scoped resource access and retention/export policy.

revocation.mechanism: Remove store role and app permission, block access and verify existing sessions.
revocation.residualAccess: Cached/exported records need separate incident handling.

edges.permission: Approve regional key lifecycle separately from payload-reader permission.
edges.credential: Separately controlled key-administration identity and approved key custody.
edges.delegation: Regional key authority approves rotation/recovery; exclusivity unresolved.

revocation.mechanism: Revoke key-administrator access and rotate/recover only through safety-reviewed service procedure.
revocation.residualAccess: Service availability/recovery keys and already decrypted data are not eliminated by tenant topology.

indirectPaths.meaning: Hybrid source compromise may affect workforce app access through synchronized state; a second app region is not identity independence.
A deployment identity can indirectly affect data through deployed code, despite lacking direct data-reader rights; release review is a privilege-path control.

forbiddenPaths: Regional app admin → tenant-wide identity/key/baseline administration
CI workload → tenant role grants or external trusted-baseline writes
Normal on-premises IdP or cloud-only password vault → exclusive custody of emergency methods
EU raw telemetry → unrestricted global analyst workspace

edges.alternative: Second separately controlled emergency account, still cloud dependent.

edges.dependency: Cloud auth, DNS/time/network and management APIs are reachable.
edges.failureEffect: No cloud administration; full cloud outage outside R1/R3.
edges.alternative: Wait/escalate service incident; no fictional offline Entra login.

edges.failureEffect: Emergency account exists but is unusable.

edges.failureEffect: Unknown state may reintroduce malicious change.

edges.alternative: Manually reauthorize only explicit owner-approved edges; mark gap.

edges.alternative: Witnessed offline log until approved evidence retrieval resumes.

edges.failureEffect: If method is stored only here, bootstrap is circular.
edges.alternative: Do not use the normal vault as sole emergency custody.

edges.failureEffect: Normal authentication failure can block emergency authentication.
edges.alternative: E1-R-CUSTODY removes this proposed dependency; demonstrate before reliance.

restorationOrder: Verify independent authority/custody and reachable cloud APIs
Retrieve independently trusted baseline and logs

alternatives.name: One tenant with regional data/application scopes
alternatives.reason: Matches the declared shared-identity acceptance without adding unjustified tenants; regional service/legal fit and recovery still need proof.

alternatives.name: Tenant per region with shared corporate administrators
alternatives.reason: No declared mandatory requirement demands extra tenants, and shared administrator identities would retain a common authority path.

alternatives.name: S3 local identity at each office
alternatives.reason: Autonomous industrial-style local operation is not required by the office workload and is not justified by the S1 scenario.

Would need a different continuity and cost review.

topology.summary: One tenant with scoped controls, subject to all declared mandatory gates.

identity.summary: Shared authority may be acceptable only within the declared containment requirements.

connectivity.summary: S1 describes required function and duration, not proven uptime or tenant count.

readiness.summary: All applicable prerequisites must be satisfied. Declarations are self-reported, not inspected or operationally verified. A candidate is not deployment approval; maturity labels are not readiness evidence.

assumptions: Inputs describe the proposed configuration and are self-reported; no tenant, configuration, authority graph, evidence file or live service has been inspected.
The one-tenant fit declaration concerns actual mandatory requirements, not acquisition frequency, legal labels, key ownership or organizational preference alone.
S0-S4 are continuity requirements; T1-T3 are tenant/authority patterns, T4 is a disconnected operating overlay, and T5 is a time-bounded transition pattern.
No security risk, cost, availability guarantee, legal approval or safety certification is calculated.
